title: Affine global Hom scalar extension out of a proper flat perfect direct image
statement: Let Y,Y′ be affine qcqs schemes, X qcqs, f:X→Y proper flat locally of finite presentation, g:Y′→Y arbitrary, M∈D_QCoh(X) perfect and K∈D_QCoh(Y) arbitrary [def-pc-perfect-complex, def-pc-derived-category]. For independent sheaf and module derived localization universes, the transpose under global derived scalar extension/restriction of the canonical mixed pullback global Hom comparison at (Rf_*M,K) [lem-sc-flat-affine-global-hom-comparison] is an isomorphism. No right adjoint or right-adjoint base-change map occurs.

source.place: Tag 0AA8, right-hand-side computation case (1); Tags 0A1H, 0B91 and 0A6A

proof.text: Compute first in standard K-injective derived localizations, including all open sites, and transport along localization equivalences. Proper-support perfect direct image applied to M and O_X concentrated in degree zero gives Rf_*M perfect: flatness makes O_X relatively flat, local finite presentation gives finite presentation, properness supplies proper support, and the tensor unitor removes O_X.

On the affine bases replace Rf_*M by a bounded finite-projective complex P over A=Γ(Y), and K by an arbitrary complex Q. Perfect RHom base change identifies the derived scalar extension of Hom(P,Q) with Hom(A′ tensor P,A′ tensor Q).

The affine derived equivalences identify pullback with scalar extension. The K-flat tensorator equation and evaluation-mate equation identify the transpose of the algebraic map with mixedGlobalHomPullbackComparison; normalized Leray is identified by its derived-unit equation. Localization uniqueness transports this identification to the supplied independent derived universes. The displayed map is therefore the perfect RHom base-change isomorphism.
